title: WSI de-identification re-scan policy + label/macro PHI quarantine spec
context: Whole-slide image files (SVS, DICOM, OME-TIFF) can carry burned-in patient identifiers in their label images, macro images, associated/auxiliary images, embedded metadata fields (e.g. SVS ImageDescription, DICOM tags), and even filenames. Even nominally de-identified public collections (TCGA, CPTAC) warrant a defensive re-scan before any derived tile, thumbnail, or feature is produced or redistributed. This policy must be defined before any collection is ingested (M0, cold-start) and must specify screening scope, deidStatus values, the quarantine workflow, and the rule that no derived artifact is produced from an unscanned slide. See PLAN.md (De-identification stance).
objective: Author the WSI de-identification re-scan policy and label/macro PHI quarantine specification: define what is extracted and screened (label image, macro image, associated/auxiliary images, embedded metadata, filenames), the screening methods (OCR + text/face heuristics), the deidStatus states (passed|quarantined|manual-cleared), the quarantine workflow (auto-quarantine on any positive, manual-review SLA, nothing redistributed unscanned), and the hard rule that slide-label and macro images are never published.
acceptanceCriteria: Policy specifies extraction and screening of each WSI label image, macro image, and associated/auxiliary images using OCR and text/face heuristics.
Policy specifies scanning of filenames and embedded metadata fields (SVS ImageDescription, DICOM tags) for identifiers.
Three deidStatus values are defined: passed, quarantined, manual-cleared; semantics and transitions are specified.
Quarantine workflow defined: any positive hit triggers automatic quarantine, a manual-review SLA is stated, and the slide is excluded from all derived artifacts until cleared.
Hard rule stated: no derived artifact (tile, thumbnail, feature) is produced or redistributed from an unscanned slide.
Hard rule stated: slide-label and macro images are never published in any artifact.
Policy is structured as a committed document (e.g. gate/deid/policy.md or docs/deid-policy.md) with a PR.
output: A WSI de-identification re-scan policy document (committed via PR) specifying screening scope, methods, deidStatus states, quarantine workflow, manual-review SLA, and the no-unscanned-derivative and no-label/macro-publication rules.
